name: GRM
job: Measures how well a genome predicts a laboratory susceptibility result. Only its evaluation terms, the assumptions a report figure rests on and aggregate counts are exported.
binding_note: Written by GRM's scripts/givens-export/export.py from the repository's documents and committed summary files. Each count is read from a committed file or quoted from a document, and an entry GRM has not counted says so. The file names no dataset, species, antibiotic, sequence, variant or gene. GRM reads nothing from Givens.

nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.definition: One species with one antibiotic, and the genomes that have a reported laboratory call for it.

quotes.quote: A dataset is one species and one antibiotic.

measured.what: curated datasets that have a report in the release the site serves
measured.quote: Of its 277 curated datasets, 274 have a report and 3 have none, because one class is under the minimum of 25 genomes.

nodes.label: Report figure
nodes.definition: A learner's sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, very major error rate or major error rate from cross-validation, as a dataset report states it.

quotes.quote: Each dataset report gives a learner's sensitivity and specificity from cross-validation on the cohort.
The headline learner has the best random-split balanced accuracy (the mean of sensitivity and specificity) among learners scored on every isolate on every split that ran
a two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson (exact binomial) interval for VME, over the resistant isolates the row called

measured.what: error-rate counts in the release's interval files that differ from the count rebuilt from the released index

nodes.label: Split
nodes.definition: How a dataset's genomes are divided into folds for cross-validation. Each learner is cross-validated on two splits.

quotes.quote: Each learner is cross-validated on two splits.

nodes.label: Random split
nodes.definition: Stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with each fold keeping the dataset's mix of resistant and susceptible genomes.

quotes.quote: The random split is stratified 5-fold cross-validation, the scheme most published numbers use, with each fold keeping the dataset's R/S mix.

measured.what: datasets whose report has a random split

nodes.label: Lineage split
nodes.definition: Folds that hold out whole lineage clusters, so a test genome has no near-identical relative in training. It is the stricter of the two splits.

quotes.quote: The lineage split holds out whole lineage clusters, so a test genome has no near-identical relative in training
The lineage split is the stricter of the two splits, because it holds out whole lineages.

measured.what: datasets whose report has a lineage split

nodes.label: Duplicate group
nodes.definition: The genomes of one dataset that have the same k-mer set. From revision 10 the random split keeps each group whole in one test fold.

quotes.quote: From revision 10, the random split keeps each group of k-mer-identical genomes whole in one outer test fold

nodes.label: Evaluation revision
nodes.definition: The numbered version of the scoring rules a report was computed under. A figure is read with its split and its revision.

quotes.quote: Read each learner's figures with their split and their evaluation revision.

nodes.label: Outside-study population
nodes.definition: Newly deposited genomes from the same database, scored by a report's final model, unchanged. It is a retrospective test on newly deposited studies from the same database, and it is no external validation.

quotes.quote: This is the result of a retrospective test on newly deposited studies from the same database.
The test is not a lockbox, and it is not external validation.

nodes.label: Studies the cohort does not hold
nodes.definition: New genomes from studies the cohort does not hold. The plan's first population.

quotes.quote: The test asks whether the lineage-split figures hold when the report's final model is applied, unchanged, to genomes from studies the cohort does not hold.

measured.what: datasets of the population that can be read against a report figure

read.count: web/src/data/outside-study.json: rows of population primary, learner scm, that are read

read.of: web/src/data/outside-study.json: genomes frozen of population primary

measured.note: A total with no denominator. The export names no species.

nodes.label: Studies the cohort already holds
nodes.definition: New genomes from studies the cohort already holds. The plan scores this population apart from the first.

quotes.quote: Its genomes are new, and they come from studies the cohort already holds.
The plan scores them apart and does not compare them, so setting them side by side was added after both results were read.

read.of: web/src/data/outside-study.json: genomes frozen of population same-study

nodes.label: Reading
nodes.definition: How a report figure compares with the estimate on new genomes: below, consistent or above. Sensitivity and specificity are read one at a time.

quotes.quote: The plan reads sensitivity and specificity one at a time.

nodes.label: Holds
nodes.definition: Neither the learner's sensitivity nor its specificity reads below on the dataset.

quotes.quote: This document also joins them: a learner holds on a dataset when neither its sensitivity nor its specificity reads below.

nodes.label: Below
nodes.definition: The report's figure is above the whole 95% interval of the new estimate. It is a measured comparison, and figures move both ways.

quotes.quote: A reading is "below" when the report's figure is above the whole 95% interval of the new estimate.
For the set covering machine, sensitivity reads above the report's figure on 36 of the 81 datasets and below it on 27.

measured.what: datasets on which the set covering machine's sensitivity reads above the report's figure, on genomes from studies the cohort does not hold

read.count: web/src/data/outside-study.json: rows of population primary, learner scm, whose sensitivity reads above
read.of: web/src/data/outside-study.json: rows of population primary, learner scm, that are read

read.count: web/src/data/outside-study.json: rows of population primary, learner scm, whose sensitivity reads below
read.of: web/src/data/outside-study.json: rows of population primary, learner scm, that are read

nodes.label: Not readable
nodes.definition: The report has no lineage-split figure to read against. The random split is not put in its place.

quotes.quote: A report whose lineage split is unavailable has no lineage-split estimate.
Its reading is "not read: no lineage-split estimate", and the random split is not substituted.

measured.what: datasets that cannot be read, on genomes from studies the cohort does not hold

read.count: (web/src/data/outside-study.json: datasets of population primary) - (web/src/data/outside-study.json: rows of population primary, learner scm, that are read)

nodes.label: Antibiotic vocabulary
nodes.definition: The names GRM resolves antibiotics through. GRM has its own vocabulary and needs no other, SigDrug's reviewed vocabulary can be added to it, and the report records which one was used.

quotes.quote: Antibiotic names resolve through GRM's bundled vocabulary.
the report records which vocabulary was used.

nodes.label: Learner row
nodes.definition: One learner's figures on one split of one dataset. From revision 14 each learner row covers every genome of the split.

quotes.quote: From evaluation revision 14, each learner row of a dataset report covers every genome of the split.

measured.what: learner rows in the release, of the rows that five learners on each split that ran would give

nodes.label: Best learner
nodes.definition: The learner with the best random-split balanced accuracy among learners scored on every genome on every split that ran. A dataset report names it.

quotes.quote: `report::best_learner` picks the best random-split balanced accuracy among learners scored on every isolate on every split that ran.

nodes.label: Called metrics
nodes.definition: A learner's figures over the genomes of fitted folds only. From revision 14 a learner row with a fold whose fit learned nothing beyond the class balance keeps this earlier figure beside the figure over every genome.

quotes.quote: It holds the revision-13 figure: the metrics over the genomes of fitted folds only, or `null` when every fold is null.

nodes.label: Fold scored at prevalence
nodes.definition: A fold whose fit learned nothing beyond the class balance. Revision 14 scores each of its test genomes at the fold's training prevalence.

quotes.quote: A null fit is an outer fold whose fitted model learned nothing beyond the class balance
Each test genome of a null-fit fold gets that fold's training prevalence as its score

measured.what: learner rows with at least one such fold

nodes.label: No report
nodes.definition: A curated dataset with no report, because one class is under the class minimum. The release lists each one with its reason.

quotes.quote: Of its 277 curated datasets, 274 have a report and 3 have none, because one class is under the minimum of 25 genomes.
The published report lists them in `SKIPS.json`.

measured.what: curated datasets with no report in the release the site serves
measured.quote: Of its 277 curated datasets, 274 have a report and 3 have none, because one class is under the minimum of 25 genomes.

nodes.label: Split unavailable
nodes.definition: A dataset whose lineage split could not be formed. The report records why.

quotes.quote: The lineage split is unavailable when whole lineages cannot fill outer and inner folds that each hold both classes, and the report records why.

measured.what: datasets with no lineage split

nodes.label: Label inferred from a MIC and left out
nodes.definition: A label inferred from a measured concentration. It stays in the curated data, marked, and no learner trains or is scored on it.

quotes.quote: Labels inferred from an MIC, using the MIC cutoff that best reproduces the reported calls, stay in the curated phenotypes, marked `label_from_mic`, and no learner trains or is scored on them.

measured.what: datasets with at least one genome whose label GRM inferred from a MIC and left out of training and scoring, of the datasets whose index entry records that count
measured.note: A count of datasets, read from the released index. A label is one genome and one antibiotic, so one genome can count in several datasets. The count says nothing about how any isolate should be treated.

assumptions.statement: A genome in a test fold has no copy in the training folds.
assumptions.hidden_in: Stratified random folds drawn without looking for identical genomes.
assumptions.when_false: A model is scored on a genome it trained on, and the figure reads better than the model is.

quotes.quote: Before revision 10 nothing kept copies apart. Stratified random folds could put one copy of a genome in training and the other in test.

import_rule: GRM writes this file with scripts/givens-export/export.py. Givens stores it unchanged and names the GRM commit it copied it from.
A measured line is an aggregate, and its text says what it counts. The file names no dataset, species or antibiotic.
A line with basis file is read from a committed summary file, and the export lists that file's sha256.
A line with basis document is quoted from the repository's text. No committed file rebuilds it unless the line names a suite.
An entry with unmeasured says what GRM has not counted. Givens shows that as missing and fills in no number.
A figure is read with its split, its learner and its evaluation revision. A line of revision 12 is never shown as revision 14's.
left_out: Dataset ids, species names and antibiotic names.
Rows for one species or one drug class.
GRM's features, models, panels and samples.
The known-gene rule's rows and its catalog.
MIC values and the MIC regression's figures.
How far a figure moved where the document gives it for named species only.
